subject: Request: Clarify product output ownership & training carveouts (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@novumhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Clarify product output ownership & training carveouts (MSA + Order Form)

Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novum is excited about the latency gains. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + Order Form and flagged three areas we need explicit language on before we can sign:

1) Output ownership: we need an explicit statement that Novum retains title to customer-provided data and to outputs generated by Redwood when driven by Novum content (examples: patient summaries generated from Novum records).
2) Training / model use: Novum requires an explicit opt-out for model training on their data and for any use of outputs in model improvements; training may only occur on mutually agreed, redacted datasets.
3) Feedback license: if Redwood consumes customer feedback/telemetry for product improvements, that license must be non-exclusive, aggregated, and strictly non-commercial (no derivative model training unless separately contracted).

Attached is our redline (Novum_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) with suggested language and rationale. Can your contracts/legal team propose an Order Form clause that captures a training opt-in checkbox and a narrow feedback license? Also need to confirm whether Redwood offers an explicit commercial carveout for enterprise telemetry.

Immediate ask: can we get proposed language by Tuesday (27 Apr)? We have an internal procurement window that week. Happy to take a quick call to expedite.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of AI Ops — Novum Health
[Attachment: Novum_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify product output ownership & training carveouts (MSA + Order Form)

Alex — thanks for the clear redline and the context. Appreciate the timeline.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I'll loop in Contracts and Product to propose narrow language that preserves Novum ownership of outputs while allowing Redwood to use aggregate telemetry for product improvement.
- We'll draft an Order Form checkbox/opt-in for training; default will be "opt-out" unless Novum explicitly elects to opt-in for additional modeling services.
- Legal will propose a feedback license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product quality (non-exclusive, non-transferable), and we will explicitly exclude derivative training without separate consent.

Attached is a short strawman clause from Product that we think balances both sides (proposed_orderform_clause.txt). Can you confirm if Novum's procurement would accept: (a) output ownership retained by Novum; (b) Redwood allowed to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement; (c) a separate commercial training agreement for any model retraining? If yes, I'll ask Contracts to convert into redline language by EOD Tuesday.

If helpful, I'm available for a 20-minute call tomorrow (26 Apr) 11:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Clarify product output ownership & training carveouts — Novum (ACTION: Contracts + Prod)

Folks — forwarding Novum's redline. Procurement needs proposed contract language by EOD Tuesday (27 Apr).

Key negotiation constraints from Sales/Customer success lens:
- Risk appetite: Novum is an enterprise healthcare customer — we should treat training opt-out as likely required unless they explicitly buy an advanced modeling add-on.
- Commercial impact: refusing any telemetry use will significantly increase per-token pricing. Need to present a workback showing delta if they choose full opt-out.

Suggested package to test with Legal:
1) Order Form clause (checkbox): "Customer elects to opt-in to Redwood model training: Yes / No. Default: No. If Yes, parties will execute a separate Training Addendum specifying scope and data handling."
2) Output ownership: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer-Generated Outputs. Redwood is granted a limited license to store and process Outputs solely to provide the Service and for performance monitoring/bug fixes."
3) Feedback license narrow language: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable, worldwide license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and usage metrics for the purpose of improving the Service and Related Products; such data will not be used to train customer-facing model outputs or sold as a raw dataset."

Please turn this into redline-ready language and call out any unacceptable legal exposure (esp. re: derivative claims and PHI risk). Rishi — can you prioritize? Laura — please coordinate final redline; Grace — will need an ops note describing how opt-out changes ingestion/retention flows.

Thanks — Marissa
[Inline: suggested clause snippets]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@novumhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@novumhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify product output ownership & training carveouts (MSA + Order Form)

Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear proposed approach. Novum's legal reviewed the three-part package you surfaced and provided the following feedback:

• Output ownership: acceptable — please insert explicit "Customer retains title to outputs" phrase in MSA Section 4.2.
• Training opt-in: Novum will accept Order Form checkbox defaulted to "No". If Novum opts in later, parties will sign a separate Training Addendum.
• Feedback license: narrow language is fine but Novum requires an explicit non-derivative covenant: "Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer-Generated Outputs to create derivative models or to seed model training without a separately executed agreement."

If Redwood can add that single-sentence non-derivative covenant to the feedback clause and provide a redline of the MSA + Order Form, we can proceed to signature. I've attached a placeholder DocuSign order form (Novum_signed_orderform.pdf) — once we receive your redline we can route for internal procurement approval.

Want to keep this tight — procurement is targeting signature by next week.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of AI Ops — Novum Health
[Attachment: Novum_signed_orderform.pdf (pdf)]
